results.question: what happens now?
results.description: 90 minutes up, scores level — heading to extra time
results.response:
Okay so France just tied it 2-2 with nine minutes left in regulation. Think of this like an NBA game where the underdog just hit a clutch three to tie it with two minutes on the clock. Argentina had been up but Mbappe is going nuclear right now.

Here's what happens: they play until the 90th minute plus whatever injury time the ref adds, usually two to five extra minutes. If it's still tied after that, they go to extra time — two fifteen minute periods, like overtime in the playoffs. If STILL tied after thirty more minutes, it goes to penalty kicks. That's basically a shootout where five guys from each team take turns trying to score one-on-one against the goalie. Argentina cannot afford to let France build momentum here because Mbappe is basically playing like prime LeBron in an elimination game.

results.question: explain penalty shootouts to me
results.description: About to go to penalty shootout in the World Cup Final
results.response: Okay so this is going to a penalty shootout, which is basically soccer's version of overtime in the NFL playoffs — except way more brutal. Each team picks five guys to take one-on-one shots against the keeper from 12 yards out. They alternate back and forth. If it's still tied after five each, it goes sudden death until someone misses. Here's the thing though — this is WAY more stressful than NFL field goals. Kickers make field goals from this distance like 95 percent of the time, but penalty shootout success drops to around 75 percent because the pressure is insane. Guys who never miss in practice suddenly can't handle it. It's basically a coin flip to decide a World Cup final, which is why fans and players hate it but also why it's absolutely riveting television.
